item.title: code-modernization: version 1.0.0, usage counts and a README results table
item.description: The plugin now has a version and a changelog. item.title: code-modernization: rename the pane's rule review command to /modernize-review-pane
item.description: The pane's bare /modernize-review took the name of the plugin's own review command, so typing the short form in a pane-enabled session opened the pane's cards instead of the pop-up review. The pane's version is now /modernize-review-pane, and /modernize-review always runs the plugin command. Both st

item.title: code-modernization: a rule is tested only if a test that ran backs it
item.description: A rule named only by a skipped or pending test no longer counts as covered. It is listed as "named, not run" and fails the rules check. A test-only folder is listed as tooling and gets no verdict. The verify command tries malformed records only when the person asked for exact behavior, so a proof lo

item.title: code-modernization: approve a difference once per input
item.description: An independent check of a rewritten batch job found differences on two new inputs of one family (a blank numeric field the rewrite rejects on purpose and the old program reads as zero). Each input has several output files, so accepting the deviation meant three or four hand-written entries per input

item.title: code-modernization: make rule consolidation auditable and injection-safe
item.description: Follow-ups from review of the consolidation pass: - The agent is a restricted type with the same read-only wording as its siblings, and every field on its numbered list is a single bounded line, so a rule name containing a newline cannot fake another entry. - A group with any number out of rang

item.title: code-modernization: an uplift is not proven by a typed baseline or edited tests
item.description: Three ways a same-technology uplift could come out PROVEN too easily: - The baseline came from a table someone typed. It now counts as measured only when the script can read per-test results (JUnit or TRX XML, a runner log with a summary line, or per-test JSON) from analysis/<system>/baseline/
